hints: Use integration by parts with the inverse tangent as the part to differentiate.
The remaining integral is $\int 2x/(4+x^2)\,dx$, which is logarithmic.
Evaluate the completed antiderivative at $2$ and $0$, using $\tan^{-1}1=\pi/4$ and exact logarithm laws.
walkthrough:
Set up integration by parts for $\int_0^2 \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$ using $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$:
Let $u = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right) \implies \mathrm{d}u = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{1 + \left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{1 + \frac{1}{4}x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{2}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$
Let $\mathrm{d}v = 1\,\mathrm{d}x \implies v = x$

Apply the integration by parts formula:
$$\int_0^2 \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[x\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\right]_0^2 - \int_0^2 \dfrac{2x}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Evaluate the boundary term $\left[x\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\right]_0^2$:
At $x = 2$: $2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}(2)\right) = 2\tan^{-1}(1) = 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
At $x = 0$: $0\tan^{-1}(0) = 0$
So the integrated term equals $\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Evaluate the remaining integral $\int_0^2 \dfrac{2x}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$:
Notice that the numerator $2x$ is the derivative of the denominator $4 + x^2$, so:
$$\int_0^2 \dfrac{2x}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[\ln(4 + x^2)\right]_0^2$$

Combine the two parts to state the exact value:
$$\int_0^2 \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \ln 2$$

ai_rubric.Integration: Integration begins with $ax\tan^{-1}(\frac12x)+b\int\frac{x}{c+x^2}\,dx$. Completes integration to $x\tan^{-1}(\frac12x)-\ln(4+x^2)$. Concludes with $\frac\pi2-\ln2$.
